title: Unity Anchor
concept: Pressure from outside the relationship — family disapproval, minority stress, being judged as a couple — gets named as the shared problem, not filed as a flaw in either of you or in the relationship itself.
whenToUse: When disapproval, discrimination, or outsider judgment (family, community, strangers) is putting pressure on the two of you, and it's starting to look like a problem between you instead of a problem coming from outside.
steps: Name the stressor out loud as external: "That's coming from them, not from us."
Ask what's actually needed right now — reassurance, a plan, or just to vent.
Decide the response as a team, not solo.
Pause before reacting to the outside pressure itself.
Ask: is this about us, or about their disapproval landing on us?
State the unit out loud — "We're on the same side of this."
If it's a recurring source, decide together how much access they get, and log it at your next Weekly Reset.

phrases.text: That's coming from them, not from us.
We're on the same side of this.
What do you actually need right now — reassurance, a plan, or just to vent?

working: A recurring comment from family lands on one partner. Instead of debating whether it's a fair criticism, you name it as outside pressure, check what's needed, and decide together how much access that person gets going forward.
notWorking: Treating the outside pressure as evidence about the relationship — relitigating whether the disapproval has a point, or letting one partner absorb it alone while the other stays neutral.
activity: Name one recurring source of outside pressure on your relationship. Practice the phrase "We're on the same side of this" out loud. Agree on one thing you'll do differently the next time it comes up.
